conviction_note: Weak negative lean (p_up 44 on an abs move of 6.5, so -0.78 scaled) against a findings sum of -2.1. The main case: Q3 US comps lap the +5.2% of Q3 2025, and the FY 'low single digit' US comp guide needs roughly 1.5-2% in H2 after a 0.5% H1. The new CEO's first print is a natural moment to cut that guide. Against it: management had seen about five weeks of Q3, including the North American World Cup, when it held the guide on 2026-07-20. The US-comp bar cannot be sourced, the 25d put skew of +4.75 already leans the same way, and the 5-day run-up is +5.4%. All three pull p_up toward 50.
bar: US same-store-sales consensus: unsourced; no current Q3 2026 figure was found from Zacks, StreetAccount, LSEG or Visible Alpha. EPS bar ~$4.36 from one source (https://fn2.ai/earnings/dpz/2026-q2, page dated 2026-07-31), against $4.535/$1.209B revenue from another (Fintool, via search snippet), so the EPS bar disagrees across sources. Company guide: FY2026 US comps 'low single digits' ex-53rd week, international low single digits, operating income mid-to-high single digit ex-FX, maintained on 2026-07-20 (https://www.tradingview.com/news/marketbeat:86ccc8664094b:0-domino-s-pizza-q2-earnings-call-highlights/). Every finding is capped small because the comp bar is unsourced. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,594,111 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement = 7.8% of shares outstanding, 3.11 days to cover (equibles.com/stocks/dpz/shortinterest, via the sweep row, read 2026-10-12). That is elevated but not crowded, down from 8.1% / 2.72m shares in March 2026 (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/investors-cautious-domino-pizza-stock-135322398.html). Baseline: 25d skew +4.75 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.89, event-implied move 6.13%, run-up +5.38% over 5 days and -3.25% over 20 days, -28.6% from the 52-week high. The skew agrees with my negative sign, so part of it is probably priced. Squeeze risk is moderate, not a reason to flip the sign.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 US comps (12 weeks from 2026-06-15 to early September) lap +5.2% in Q3 2025, the hardest compare of the year. On the two-year stacks the company has reported (Q2 2026 +0.1% on +3.4% = 3.5; Q1 2026 +0.9%), Q3 points to roughly -2% to +1%. Industry traffic was negative throughout the quarter: Placer.ai QSR visits -3.7% YoY in August and -2.2% in September, the seventh straight monthly decline, with record September gas prices squeezing price-sensitive QSR customers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A US comp miss is punished: 2026-04-27 US comps +0.9% vs ~2.5% expected plus a guide cut gave -8.84%. 2026-07-20 (US comps +0.1%, EPS miss, revenue beat) opened about +8% premarket and closed +2.11%, so good news gets sold intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: The compare is public, so it is partly priced; the put skew (+4.75) and the -28.6% drawdown show that. What is not visibly in the price is the size. If the Street held a Q3 US comp around 0% or below, Q2-style 'misses' would not be possible. The last datapoints found (Kalshi July market ~59% odds of >2%; Bloomberg Intelligence saying Q2/Q3 comp expectations 'may still be too elevated') suggest the bar sits above the two-year-stack arithmetic. I could not source a current consensus, so this stays small.
findings.independence: Placer.ai September 2026 index, a different source and an industry proxy: https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/september-2026-retail-and-dining-index-shoppers-keep-showing-up-despite-record-gas-prices (2026-10-12). Pizza peer weakness through Q2: Papa John's NA comps -8.3% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000901491/000162828026053810/pzza-62826xpressrelease.htm, 2026-08-06). Q2 two-year stack from DPZ's Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286681/000128668126000034/dpz-ex99_1.htm

findings.finding: On 2026-07-20 the company kept its FY2026 US comp guide at 'low single digits' (ex-53rd week) and international at low single digits. H1 printed US +0.9% and +0.1% and international -0.2%. Q3 laps +5.2%, so holding even ~1% for the year needs a strong Q4. The 2026-10-13 print is Joe Jordan's first as CEO (effective 2026-10-01), which is the usual moment to reset the FY comp guide and possibly the international and unit-growth outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-27: US comp guide cut from ~3% to 'low single digits' together with a comp miss, -8.84%, the largest reaction in the 7-print history. On 2026-07-20 the guide was held, and the stock rose +2.11% after +8% premarket.
findings.why_not_priced: If a guide cut were fully expected, the stock would have no premarket-style upside left and the 5-day tape would not show a +5.4% bounce into the print. A rebound into the release suggests some holders are leaning on 'guide held'. The put skew says the downside is partly paid for. A new CEO's incentive to rebase is not a number any consensus carries.
findings.independence: CEO change confirmed in the NRN article of 2026-10-05 (https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/domino-s-flexes-its-promotional-muscle-for-national-pizza-month). The H1 comps come from the company's own Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001286681/000128668126000034/dpz-ex99_1.htm), the same document family as finding 1, so the H1 arithmetic is counted once here and the Q3 compare once in finding 1.

findings.finding: Domino's Pizza Enterprises (ASX: DMP, the largest DPZ international master franchisee) reported group SSS of -5.8% for the first 8 weeks of FY27 to 23 August 2026, after -5.7% in H2 FY26, and said 'trading remains below expectations'. That holds DPZ's international comp (H1 -0.2%) under its low-single-digit FY guide, partly offset by DPG UK H1 LFL +4.9% and a World Cup lift into July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International comps have not been the reaction driver in the baseline's history. The April and July moves were attributed to US comps and guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a foreign master franchisee's slide 17 trading update, not on US wire previews for DPZ. However, DMP's run-rate has been negative all year and was already inside DPZ's H1 -0.2%, so the new information is only that it did not improve. Sized small.
findings.independence: Offsetting: DPG UK H1 2026 LFL +4.9%, with momentum into July (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/dominos-pizza-enjoys-world-cup-boost-interim-sales-and-orders-rise, 2026-08-04). Net of the rest of international, this is a small negative.

findings.finding: The North American-hosted FIFA World Cup (2026-06-11 to 07-19) falls almost entirely inside DPZ's fiscal Q3. Deliverect reports pizza was the most-ordered meal of the tournament and US app food purchases were +55% during the final. DPZ moved Stuffed Crust into its 'Best Deal Ever' Q3 calendar and said early customer reaction supported the change. Management had ~5 weeks of Q3 in hand when it held the FY guide on 2026-07-20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Positive comp surprises have been sold intraday (2026-07-20: +8% premarket to +2.11% close; 2025-10-14 Q3 2025 +5.2% comp beat: +3.91%), so the upside is damped.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews anchor on the +5.2% compare and the Q2 ticket miss, and none I found credit a US World Cup lift to DPZ's Q3. If the market priced it, the put skew would not be +4.75 vol points into a quarter management had partly seen.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary (Stuffed Crust added to Best Deal Ever, guide held): https://www.tradingview.com/news/marketbeat:86ccc8664094b:0-domino-s-pizza-q2-earnings-call-highlights/. DPG UK credited the World Cup for H1 and July: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/dominos-pizza-enjoys-world-cup-boost-interim-sales-and-orders-rise. This is an industry proxy that DPZ has not confirmed for the US.

findings.finding: Domino's ran 50% off all pizzas, including the new premium 'Domino', from 2026-10-05 to 10-11, right after the new CEO took over. Taken with the August 31 launch of 'The Domino' and the 'Is the Domino Worthy?' $1m free-pizza receipt promotion, this reads as escalating promotional intensity entering Q4 in a category NRN calls aggressively competitive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction tied to a promotion announcement. The 2026-07-20 ticket miss shows the market cares about ticket/mix, which deep discounting pressures.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public consumer marketing, not an analyst datapoint. It matters only if the call frames Q4 ticket pressure or franchisee margin, which nobody can see yet. It is an inference, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Product launch dates: https://ir.dominos.com/node/24841. The signal is ambiguous: the former CEO framed deal intensity as a share-gain weapon ('bring it on').

baseline_tension: My negative lean agrees with the +4.75 put skew and the 28.6% drawdown, so it is probably partly priced. It cuts against the +5.4% 5-day bounce into the print. This name sells good news (July +8% premarket to +2.1%) and punishes guide cuts (April -8.8%), which keeps the asymmetry modestly negative.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced): the Q3 US-comp finding depends on an unsourced consensus, so it was capped from -1.0 to -0.7. p_up moved from 42 to 44.
Rule 9 (net of the rest): the DMP international finding was netted against DPG UK's +4.9% LFL and the World Cup lift, from -0.4 to -0.3.

Rule 5 (proxy is small): the World Cup / Deliverect finding is an unconfirmed industry proxy for the US, trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6. It is kept because the company held its guide with ~5 weeks of Q3 in hand.

Rules 1 and 7 left the guidance finding at -1.5: the skew agrees with it and short interest (7.8%, 3.1 days) is not crowded, so no extra cut and no flip. The reaction history (beats sold, guide cuts punished) supports keeping it the largest finding.
